claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain and toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr activates multiple dislocation slip systems.
Severe lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes nano-twinning during high-temperature deformation.
The combination of additional slip and twinning enhances work hardening, supplies additional plastic-deformation channels, and delays failure.
Pure tungsten has limited slip and intrinsic brittleness relative to the proposed WTaTiVZr alloy.
Mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering can produce equimolar WTaTiVZr as a single-phase, highly distorted BCC solid solution.
A controlled elevated-temperature mechanical comparison can be made between TaTiVWZr and pure tungsten.
Testing at 800–1000 °C under constant strain rate in an inert atmosphere represents sustained plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The relevant structural mediator is a high density of activated dislocation slip systems and nano-twins arising from lattice distortion.
Large atomic-size differences and the multi-principal-element composition create significant lattice distortion that impedes dislocation motion and raises internal stress.
Elevated internal stresses in WTaTiVZr promote nano-twin formation under high-temperature loading.
A high density of deformation twins can hinder dislocation motion and generate strain hardening while also contributing to ductility and more homogeneous plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten's high ductile-to-brittle transition temperature leaves it with fewer plasticity mechanisms and lower toughness under the stated conditions.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr is expected to have greater elongation, a higher strain-hardening response, and higher fracture energy.
Thermally activated dislocation processes dominate the proposed mechanism at 800–1000 °C.
The proposed mechanism is contingent on WTaTiVZr retaining a single-phase BCC structure with minimal secondary-phase formation.
Precipitates or grain-boundary segregation caused by processing variations may alter the proposed mechanism.
Elevated-temperature nano-indentation creep behavior of TaTiVWZr has previously been evaluated and its creep parameters compared with pure tungsten.
Failure to observe higher plastic strain, increased strain hardening, or a high density of nano-twins in WTaTiVZr relative to tungsten would falsify the proposed mechanism.
